reader.summary: During the week of October 17 to 24, 2026, Typhoon Champi, supercharged by El Niño conditions, battered Taiwan, killing one person, injuring over 500, cutting power to 56,000 households, and forcing the closure of schools, businesses, and the stock market while nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled. The storm then moved on to Japan and China. In the Strait of Taiwan and the western Pacific, China intensified what Taipei called grey zone and hybrid warfare tactics: 16 Chinese ships were driven away from Taiwan's waters, militia boats were accused of expanding battlefield preparation, and Beijing declared it was safeguarding order around a Taiwan-controlled South China Sea atoll. A US Congress-appointed official called Chinese patrols to Taiwan's east destabilising. On the industrial front, TSMC halted some construction after a mishap killed four workers, and Micron's Taoyuan plant workers rejected a proposed bonus and staged a one-day strike before management unveiled a global profit-linked bonus plan. The financial regulator blocked Grab's roughly 600 million dollar acquisition of Foodpanda's Taiwan delivery business. Five people were indicted for attempting to injure a comedian known for satirising Xi Jinping. September export orders hit a record on strong AI demand, and the Philippines explored deeper cooperation with Taiwan on protecting undersea cables.

display.eli5:
Last week, a huge typhoon called Champi slammed into Taiwan, knocking out power for tens of thousands of families and shutting down schools, businesses, and the stock market. The storm is gone now, but the government still has to figure out how much everything cost and how to help the people who lost electricity and property.

At the same time, China has been sending more and more ships close to Taiwan's coast, and a US government person called the whole thing destabilising. Next week, expect Beijing to push back harder, maybe with more ships or a new patrol exercise, which could make the waters around Taiwan even more tense.

On top of that, four construction workers died at a TSMC building site, and the company stopped some work. The government will probably order a full safety check, and workers' groups will push for answers about what went wrong.

A surprise would be if the blocked Grab-Foodpanda delivery deal turns into a bigger fight about how much foreign companies can own in Taiwan's food delivery market.
